cause_quote: The first delegated candidate admission added `process.ppid !== parent.lease.executor.pid ||` to its rejection conditions, so a Windows candidate with a different immediate parent PID was refused even when its lease was valid.
user_saw: A Windows update could stop with “Candidate executor binding does not match its parent” even though the update owner and candidate lease were current.
summary: The fix admits Windows candidates using their live executor lease identity and still requires a direct parent when the candidate cannot read its own process identity.
reasoning: The introducing diff added delegated executor admission, wired it into the Windows-capable update continuation, and imposed the immediate-parent PID check from the start. Later commits changed the comparison to use the recorded spawner and moved it into the grant module while preserving the same rejection for Windows candidates with different launcher ancestry.
